title: Canonical derived scalar-extension and cotangent base-change maps for ring squares
statement: Let $A\xrightarrow{f}C$, $A'\xrightarrow{g}C'$, $a:A\to A'$ and $c:C\to C'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with $c\circ f=g\circ a$, and denote this square by $q$. Write $D(R)$ for the derived category of ordinary $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a ring map $h:R\to S$, define $L_h:D(R)\to D(S)$ as the universal total left derived functor of termwise extension of scalars $M\mapsto M\otimes_R S$ [def-weil-module-base-change], and use the derived tensor/restriction adjunction $L_h\dashv\operatorname{Res}_h$ induced by the ordinary tensor/restriction adjunction and the canonical exact-restriction comparison. Define $s_q:C\to\operatorname{Res}_a\operatorname{Res}_g C'$ to be the $A$-linear map $x\mapsto c(x)$, with $C$ viewed as an $A$-module through $f$. Define the canonical multiplication $\mu_q:L_a(C[0])\to (\operatorname{Res}_g C')[0]$ in $D(A')$ to be the adjoint of $s_q[0]$ under this normalized adjunction, using the canonical comparison between restriction of scalars and the degree-zero embedding. For the standard cotangent complexes and square functoriality map $t_q:L_{C/A}\to\operatorname{Res}_c L_{C'/A'}$ [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], define the canonical cotangent base-change morphism $\beta_q:L_c(L_{C/A})\to L_{C'/A'}$ in $D(C')$ to be the adjoint of $t_q$ under the same normalized derived tensor/restriction adjunction. These constructions require no flatness, Tor-vanishing or invertibility assumption on the square.
